title: Gnocchi with Brown Butter and Sage

steps.title: Tools
steps.instruction: Pull out a large pan for boiling, a frying pan, a slotted spoon, a knife and board, and something to zest a lemon with.

steps.title: Prep
steps.instruction: Before any heat: slice the garlic finely, pick the sage leaves off their stems, and zest the lemon.

steps.title: Water on
steps.instruction: Fill a large pan with water, salt it well, and put it on high. It goes on first because it is the slowest thing here. Tell me when it is at a rolling boil.
steps.visualCheck: A rolling boil is big bubbles breaking across the whole surface, not a few rising from the bottom.

steps.title: Boil, then lift out
steps.instruction: Drop the gnocchi into the boiling water. They are done the moment they float, about 2 minutes, and they come straight out with the slotted spoon into a bowl. Do not wait for me: when they float, lift them.
steps.visualCheck: They sink at first, then rise and bob on the surface, and it happens all at once. Floating is the signal. Leave them in after that and they go gluey.
steps.recovery: If they have been swimming a while and feel soft, get them out now and be gentle with them in the pan. They will still crisp up.

steps.title: Oil in, bring the pan up to heat
steps.instruction: Frying pan on medium-high, then 2 tbsp of olive oil straight in, and let it come up for a minute or two. Before the gnocchi go anywhere near it, flick in two or three drops of water and watch what they do. Tell me when the pan is ready.
steps.visualCheck: Ready is when the drops skitter and bead across the surface and take a second or two to go. If they sit and steam it is not hot enough yet. If they vanish instantly with a sharp crack it is too hot.
steps.recovery: Too hot is the one to fix, because the same pan browns the butter later and a pan that is too hot burns it. Take it off the heat for thirty seconds and test again.

steps.title: Fry the gnocchi
steps.instruction: Gnocchi into the hot oil with a pinch of salt and pepper. Five to six minutes, turning them so they colour on two sides. Tell me when they are golden and I will take you on.
steps.visualCheck: Deep golden and crisp on the flat sides, still soft in the middle.
steps.recovery: If they are steaming rather than colouring the pan is crowded. Cook them in two batches instead.

steps.title: Brown the butter
steps.instruction: Gnocchi back into the bowl, and wipe the pan if anything caught. Now turn the heat DOWN to medium and let the pan settle for thirty seconds, because the pan you just fried in is too hot for butter. Test it again with a drop of water, and when it skitters rather than cracks, put 75g of butter in. Two to three minutes. Tell me when it smells nutty.
steps.visualCheck: It melts, foams up, and then the foam subsides. Watch the milk solids on the bottom: when they turn the colour of a hazelnut and it smells nutty rather than buttery, that is your moment.
steps.recovery: Black flecks and a sharp, acrid smell mean it has gone past browned to burnt, and burnt butter cannot be brought back. Tip it out, wipe the pan, and start the butter again. Losing 75g of butter is much better than serving it.

steps.title: Crisp the sage
steps.instruction: Sage leaves straight into the browned butter. About 2 minutes. Tell me when they have stopped crackling.
steps.visualCheck: They crackle when they go in, then go quiet, darken and stiffen. Crisp, not browned.

steps.title: Garlic, one minute
steps.instruction: Sliced garlic in, stirring, for one minute and no longer. Keep the heat where it is. Tell me when it smells sweet.
steps.visualCheck: Pale gold at the edges and sweet smelling. It must not go brown.
steps.recovery: Garlic in hot butter goes bitter fast. If it is colouring quickly, pull the pan off the heat and keep stirring in the residual warmth.

steps.title: Bring it together
steps.instruction: Gnocchi back into the pan with a quarter teaspoon each of salt and pepper. Stir for a minute, until everything is coated. Tell me when they are glossy.
steps.visualCheck: Every piece glossy with butter, sage through it rather than sitting on top.

steps.title: Lemon, off the heat
steps.instruction: Take the pan off the heat first, then stir through the lemon zest and the juice of half the lemon. Off the heat so the lemon stays bright instead of cooking down.

steps.title: Serve
steps.instruction: Divide between bowls and finish with grated parmesan and a good grind of black pepper. Straight to the table while the sage is still crisp.
